messages:
ana: FYI — customer Alpha is asking for 7-year audit retention + BYOK for Private. They want firm dates for Q3. Need prioritization call: cost, launch gates, and minimal acceptance criteria.

sam: 7yrs is a big ask. Two quick points: storage & search cost, and legal/retention complexity. We should estimate storage delta and decide archival strategy (cold snapshot vs indexable archive).

jordan: For Private we can design it, but it touches export pipelines and backup windowing. Long-retention implies cold-tiering and a retrieval SLA tradeoff. Ops overhead increases (restore drills, snapshot verification).

clare: From security/SOC2 angle: >1yr retention triggers additional controls. BYOK requires documented HSM/KMS escrow, rotation policy, and audit trails. Also need immutable legal-hold support for e-discovery.

mike: Ballpark numbers: storing audit events at current ingestion for 7yrs adds ~+35-50% infra cost per tenant (depends on compression and dedupe). Exports/search spikes add variable egress costs. I can get a more exact delta with retention profiles.

ana: (typo) ana: Proposed option set to present to leadership:
  A) Default 1yr, paid add-on archival up to 7yrs (recommended)
  B) 3yr enterprise tier included in higher-priced plan
  C) 7yr only for regulated/gov customers via private deployment (raise to backlog for general availability)
Which of these is technically feasible for a Q3 scoped deliverable?

sam: A makes the most sense. Implementation notes:
  - Hot index: 30 days
  - Warm tier (searchable): 30-365 days
  - Cold tier (archive & restore): >365 days, export-only or slower query path
  - Need prefix/KV caching adjustments for retention queries
  - Provide export tool + retention API as interim for big customers

jordan: Rollout suggestion: canary on Dedicated customers who opt-in -> Private customers with opt-in -> GA.
Acceptance criteria (engineering):
  - BYOK handshake automated tests pass for HSM-backed keys
  - End-to-end export & restore tested (sample datasets)
  - Search query fallback behavior documented (hot vs cold)
  - Runbook for restore and legal-hold unrelease

clare: Security/Compliance acceptance checklist (high-level):
  - KMS audit logs integrated into evidence store
  - Key rotation + revoked-key recovery plan documented
  - Pen test scope includes archive retrieval APIs
  - Legal-hold toggle immutability verified

ana: sample retention config snippet (for product/eng discussion):
```
retention_policy:
  default_days: 365
  warm_days: 30
  archival_after_days: 365
  cold_tier: s3-glacier
  legal_hold: false
  byok_required: true
```

mike: That config helps. I'll model cost scenarios for default vs 7yr by EOD tomorrow and attach numbers to the RFC. Also note licensing revenue potential for add-on archival.

sam: I'll open an RFC/PR with implementation plan + storage/compute estimates and link it here: https://git.internal/rfcs/retention-archival (WIP).

jordan: Ops: add restore drills to oncall playbook and define SLOs: hot query <2s, warm query <5s, cold export within 60s for small ranges, and full-tenant bulk export SLAs to be negotiated.

clare: Please also include SOC2/ISO evidence mapping for archival in the RFC — I'll review and sign off for compliance scope.

ana: Thanks all. Action items: @mike cost delta by EOD tomorrow, @sam RFC opened today, @clare compliance checklist added to RFC, @jordan ops runbook draft. We'll do a customer sync once RFC is in review.

mike: Ack, on it.

sam: PR created, pinged reviewers. https://git.internal/rfcs/retention-archival/pull/3

jordan: +1 on staged rollout. Ops will prepare runbook template and restore test plan.

ana: Great — closing thread for now, will follow up with schedule for the prioritization meeting. :thumbsup:
